dedupe_keys.name: norway s programme for reinforced mobile coverage forsterket ekom base stations with three day backup power in 112 municipalities

description: Norway's programme for reinforced electronic communications (forsterket ekom), run by Nkom, is a state measure to keep mobile communication working in a selected area of each participating municipality even when the power fails or the mobile network goes down. The selected area usually lies around the town hall or other buildings with important public functions, so that the municipality's crisis management and residents can make calls, send text messages and use the internet during a crisis. Selected base stations have backup power lasting up to three days and a backup transmission link if the main connection fails, so coverage can be kept much longer than normal during power cuts, fibre breaks or other incidents. The page, updated on 28 May 2026, reports 112 municipalities covered and 20 more planned for 2026, with sections on where the reinforced network is, its objectives, the requirements for base stations, new municipalities and regions under consideration, and the organisation of the programme. The programme matters most in rural municipalities and where mobile and network access is vulnerable. Coverage: Norway. Format and access: web pages with a map of where reinforced coverage exists, free. Caveats: programme descriptions, not measured performance during events; site-level data are not published. Simulation uses: backup power duration and redundant links as parameters for modelling mobile network survival in long power outages and storms. Related records: the Nkom statistics give coverage, and the Japan 2011 telecom damage case study shows why longer backup power was adopted there.
